summary: Malaysia grants visa-free entry to most nationalities — up to a month for ASEAN neighbors except Myanmar, 30 days for Chinese citizens (visa-free since 1 September 2026) and Indian citizens (exemption extended through 2026), and requires almost all foreign arrivals to submit the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) online within 3 days before travel.

vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required of travellers aged 1 year or over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, or who transited for more than 12 hours through an airport in one.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not an entry requirement, but medical coverage is recommended — private hospitals, which most visitors use, charge in full.

proofOfFunds.text: No official fixed amount is published, but you must be able to show sufficient funds for your stay if asked at the border.

declarations.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC)
declarations.text: Almost all foreign nationals must submit the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival (exemptions cover Singapore citizens using automated lanes, permanent residents and some pass holders). It is free. Use only the official Immigration Department portal.

source.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) — official portal

currencyLimits.text: Cash and bearer negotiable instruments exceeding the equivalent of USD 10,000 must be declared on arrival and departure on Customs Form No. 7. Carrying more than USD 10,000 worth of Malaysian ringgit in or out also needs prior written approval from Bank Negara Malaysia.

source.name: Royal Malaysian Customs Department — Cash and Bearer Negotiable Instrument (CBNI) Declaration
source.instrument: Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, s.28B(1); Customs Regulations 2019, reg. 55; Financial Services Act 2013, s.214(9)

notes: Duty-free allowance: 1 liter of alcohol; tobacco products are no longer duty-free at most entry points.
Drug trafficking carries the death penalty under Malaysian law — never carry packages for others.
Alcohol allowances and local rules are stricter in the states of Kelantan and Terengganu.

payments.text: Cards and e-wallets (Touch 'n Go, GrabPay) are accepted widely in cities and malls; hawker stalls, small shops, taxis and rural areas often remain cash-first. ATMs are plentiful and accept foreign cards.

safety.text: Bag-snatching is common in major cities, often by thieves on motorbikes, and credit card and ATM fraud is widespread. The UK government advises against all but essential travel to the islands and dive sites off eastern Sabah, from Sandakan to Tawau, because of the threat of kidnapping; this does not apply to the Sabah mainland.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Malaysia travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Best months depend on the coast: roughly March–September suits the west coast (Penang, Langkawi), while the east coast and its islands are best outside the November–February northeast monsoon.

idp.text: Malaysia is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Malaysia is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Malaysia yet.

tips.text: The MDAC arrival card is free. Third-party sites charging a fee for it are unnecessary and often scams. Submit it only at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac within 3 days of arrival.
Malaysia imposes the death penalty for drug trafficking and severe penalties for possession. Never carry luggage or packages for anyone else.
Plan around the monsoons: the east coast islands (Perhentian, Redang, Tioman) largely shut down from November to February, while the west coast stays open year-round.
Sabah and Sarawak (Malaysian Borneo) run their own immigration controls — your passport is checked again when flying there from Peninsular Malaysia, and a separate stay period is stamped.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Malaysia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter Malaysia without a visa; Malaysia's Immigration Department does not publish how long US citizens may stay. The only mandatory step is the free Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC), submitted online within 3 days before arrival.

faq.question: What is the MDAC and who needs it?
faq.answer: The Malaysia Digital Arrival Card is a free online arrival form at imigresen-online.imi.gov.my/mdac that almost every foreign visitor must submit within 3 days before arriving. Exemptions cover Singapore citizens using automated lanes, Malaysian permanent residents and holders of certain long-term passes.

faq.question: Can Chinese and Indian citizens visit Malaysia without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. Chinese citizens on ordinary or public affairs passports have entered visa-free for up to 30 days per entry since 1 September 2026. Indian citizens are exempt from the visa for social visits until December 31, 2026, with stays of up to 30 days. Both still need to submit the free MDAC within 3 days before arrival.

faq.question: How much does a Malaysia eVisa cost?
faq.answer: For the nationalities that need one (including Pakistani and Nigerian citizens), the single-entry tourist eVisa costs a RM105 processing charge plus a visa fee that depends on nationality and a small card or e-wallet charge, allows a stay of up to 30 days, and is normally processed within 2 to 7 business days at the official portal malaysiavisa.imi.gov.my.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Malaysia?
faq.answer: It depends on the coast. The west coast (Kuala Lumpur, Penang, Langkawi) is good most of the year, especially around March–September. Avoid the east coast islands between November and February, when the northeast monsoon brings heavy rain and many resorts close.
